hadiths.arabicText: قَالَ مَالِك ، فِي الرَّجُلِ يَبِيعُ الْبَزَّ الْمُصَنَّفَ وَيَسْتَثْنِي ثِيَابًا بِرُقُومِهَا : إِنَّهُ إِنِ اشْتَرَطَ أَنْ يَخْتَارَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ الرَّقْمَ فَلَا بَأْسَ بِهِ ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَشْتَرِطْ أَنْ يَخْتَارَ مِنْهُ حِينَ اسْتَثْنَى فَإِنِّي أَرَاهُ شَرِيكًا فِي عَدَدِ الْبَزِّ الَّذِي اشْتُرِيَ مِنْهُ ، وَذَلِكَ أَنَّ الثَّوْبَيْنِ يَكُونُ رَقْمُهُمَا سَوَاءً وَبَيْنَهُمَا تَفَاوُتٌ فِي الثَّمَنِ . قَالَ مَالِك : الْأَمْرُ عِنْدَنَا ، أَنَّهُ لَا بَأْسَ بِالشِّرْكِ وَالتَّوْلِيَةِ وَالْإِقَالَةِ مِنْهُ فِي الطَّعَامِ وَغَيْرِهِ قَبَضَ ذَلِكَ أَوْ لَمْ يَقْبِضْ ، إِذَا كَانَ ذَلِكَ بِالنَّقْدِ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ فِيهِ رِبْحٌ وَلَا وَضِيعَةٌ وَلَا تَأْخِيرٌ لِلثَّمَنِ ، فَإِنْ دَخَلَ ذَلِكَ رِبْحٌ أَوْ وَضِيعَةٌ أَوْ تَأْخِيرٌ مِنْ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا ، صَارَ بَيْعًا يُحِلُّهُ مَا يُحِلُّ الْبَيْعَ وَيُحَرِّمُهُ مَا يُحَرِّمُ الْبَيْعَ ، وَلَيْسَ بِشِرْكٍ وَلَا تَوْلِيَةٍ وَلَا إِقَالَةٍ . قَالَ مَالِك : مَنِ اشْتَرَى سِلْعَةً بَزًّا أَوْ رَقِيقًا فَبَتَّ بِهِ ثُمَّ سَأَلَهُ رَجُلٌ أَنْ يُشَرِّكَهُ فَفَعَلَ ، وَنَقَدَا الثَّمَنَ صَاحِبَ السِّلْعَةِ جَمِيعًا ثُمَّ أَدْرَكَ السِّلْعَةَ شَيْءٌ يَنْتَزِعُهَا مِنْ أَيْدِيهِمَا ، فَإِنَّ الْمُشَرَّكَ يَأْخُذُ مِنَ الَّذِي أَشْرَكَهُ الثَّمَنَ ، وَيَطْلُبُ الَّذِي أَشْرَكَ بَيِّعَهُ الَّذِي بَاعَهُ السِّلْعَةَ بِالثَّمَنِ كُلِّهِ ، إِلَّا أَنْ يَشْتَرِطَ الْمُشَرِّكُ عَلَى الَّذِي أَشْرَكَ بِحَضْرَةِ الْبَيْعِ وَعِنْدَ مُبَايَعَةِ الْبَائِعِ الْأَوَّلِ ، وَقَبْلَ أَنْ يَتَفَاوَتَ ذَلِكَ ، أَنَّ عُهْدَتَكَ عَلَى الَّذِي ابْتَعْتُ مِنْهُ ، وَإِنْ تَفَاوَتَ ذَلِكَ وَفَاتَ الْبَائِعَ الْأَوَّلَ فَشَرْطُ الْآخَرِ بَاطِلٌ وَعَلَيْهِ الْعُهْدَةُ . قَالَ مَالِك فِي الرَّجُلِ يَقُولُ لِلرَّجُلِ : اشْتَرِ هَذِهِ السِّلْعَةَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ ، وَانْقُدْ عَنِّي وَأَنَا أَبِيعُهَا لَكَ : إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَا يَصْلُحُ حِينَ قَالَ : انْقُدْ عَنِّي وَأَنَا أَبِيعُهَا لَكَ ، وَإِنَّمَا ذَلِكَ سَلَفٌ يُسْلِفُهُ إِيَّاهُ عَلَى أَنْ يَبِيعَهَا لَهُ ، وَلَوْ أَنَّ تِلْكَ السِّلْعَةَ هَلَكَتْ أَوْ فَاتَتْ ، أَخَذَ ذَلِكَ الرَّجُلُ الَّذِي نَقَدَ الثَّمَنَ مِنْ شَرِيكِهِ مَا نَقَدَ عَنْهُ ، فَهَذَا مِنَ السَّلَفِ الَّذِي يَجُرُّ مَنْفَعَةً . قَالَ مَالِك : وَلَوْ أَنَّ رَجُلًا ابْتَاعَ سِلْعَةً فَوَجَبَتْ لَهُ ، ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ رَجُلٌ : أَشْرِكْنِي بِنِصْفِ هَذِهِ السِّلْعَةِ وَأَنَا أَبِيعُهَا لَكَ جَمِيعًا ، كَانَ ذَلِكَ حَلَالًا لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ ، وَتَفْسِيرُ ذَلِكَ : أَنَّ هَذَا بَيْعٌ جَدِيدٌ بَاعَهُ نِصْفَ السِّلْعَةِ عَلَى أَنْ يَبِيعَ لَهُ النِّصْفَ الْآخَرَ .6E352
hadiths.english_translation: Malik said regarding a man who sells classified fabrics and reserves certain garments by their marks: If he stipulates that he will choose from that mark, there is no harm in it. But if he does not stipulate that he will choose from it when he reserved it, then I see him as a partner in the number of fabrics that were bought from him, because two garments may have the same mark but differ in price. Malik said: The matter with us is that there is no harm in partnership, transfer of sale, and cancellation of sale in food and other things, whether that was taken possession of or not taken possession of, if that was for cash and there was no profit or loss or delay in the price. But if profit or loss or delay from one of them enters into it, it becomes a sale that is made lawful by what makes sale lawful and forbidden by what makes sale forbidden, and it is not partnership, transfer of sale, or cancellation of sale. Malik said: Whoever buys goods, fabrics or slaves, and finalizes it, then a man asks him to make him a partner in it and he does so, and they both pay the price to the owner of the goods together, then something overtakes the goods that takes it from their hands, then the partner takes the price from the one who made him a partner, and the one who made him a partner demands from his seller who sold him the goods the entire price, unless the partner stipulates upon the one who made him a partner in the presence of the sale and at the transaction with the first seller, and before that differs, that your liability is upon the one from whom I bought. But if that differs and the first seller is gone, then the condition of the other is invalid and the liability is upon him. Malik said regarding a man who says to a man: Buy this merchandise between me and you, and pay on my behalf and I will sell it to you: That is not proper when he said: Pay on my behalf and I will sell it to you. Rather, that is a loan that he lends him on condition that he sells it to him. And if that merchandise perished or was lost, that man who paid the price would take from his partner what he paid on his behalf. So this is from the loan that draws a benefit. Malik said: If a man buys merchandise and it is confirmed for him, then a man says to him: Make me a partner in half of this merchandise and I will sell it all for you, that is permissible with no harm in it. The explanation of that is: This is a new sale in which he sold him half of the merchandise on condition that he sells the other half for him.

potential_issues.issue: This is a maqtu' narration - Malik's juristic opinion, not a prophetic hadith
potential_issues.impact: Represents Malik's ijtihad and the practice of the scholars of Madinah. While not prophetic, it carries weight as representing the consensus of Madinan jurists

hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنِي يَحْيَى ، عَنْ مَالِك ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ ، عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ الْحَارِثِ بْنِ هِشَامٍ ، أَنّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، قَالَ : " أَيُّمَا رَجُلٍ بَاعَ مَتَاعًا فَأَفْلَسَ الَّذِي ابْتَاعَهُ مِنْهُ وَلَمْ يَقْبِضْ الَّذِي بَاعَهُ مِنْ ثَمَنِهِ شَيْئًا فَوَجَدَهُ بِعَيْنِهِ ، فَهُوَ أَحَقُّ بِهِ ، وَإِنْ مَاتَ الَّذِي ابْتَاعَهُ ، فَصَاحِبُ الْمَتَاعِ فِيهِ أُسْوَةُ الْغُرَمَاءِ " 1351
hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Whichever man sells goods and the one who bought them from him becomes bankrupt, and the one who sold them has not received anything of their price, and he finds them in their exact state, then he has more right to them. But if the one who bought them dies, then the owner of the goods is equal with the creditors in them.'

chainIssues: MURSAL: Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman was a Tabi'i who never met the Prophet ﷺ
Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri uses 'an (عَنْ) - he is known for occasional tadlis
Final transmission uses 'anna (أَنَّ) indicating indirect transmission

plainChains: Yahya -> Malik -> Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri -> Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman -> (missing link) -> Prophet Muhammad ﷺ

potential_issues.issue: CRITICAL: This is a MURSAL hadith - Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman (d. 94 AH) was a Tabi'i of the Second Generation who never met the Prophet ﷺ. There is at least one missing narrator between him and the Prophet ﷺ
potential_issues.impact: Mursal hadiths are considered weak (da'if) by the majority of muhaddithun due to the unknown missing narrator(s). However, mursal narrations from reliable senior Tabi'un like Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman have some value, especially when corroborated by other chains

potential_issues.issue: Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri is classified as a mudallis (Category 3 in Ibn Hajar's classification) and uses the ambiguous term 'an (عَنْ) here
potential_issues.impact: However, al-Zuhri is unanimously considered extremely reliable (thiqah thabt) by all hadith scholars, and his 'an'anah is generally accepted. This minor concern does not significantly affect the grading given his exceptional status

potential_issues.issue: The transmission from Abu Bakr uses 'anna (أَنَّ) rather than a direct hearing term like sami'tu
potential_issues.impact: This suggests indirect transmission or that Abu Bakr heard it as a report, which compounds the mursal nature of the hadith

Topics: Rights of Seller when Buyer Becomes Bankrupt

hadiths.arabicText: وَحَدَّثَنِي مَالِك ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ سَعِيدٍ ، عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ حَزْمٍ ، عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْعَزِيزِ ، عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ الْحَارِثِ بْنِ هِشَامٍ ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ ، أَنّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، قَالَ : " أَيُّمَا رَجُلٍ أَفْلَسَ فَأَدْرَكَ الرَّجُلُ مَالَهُ بِعَيْنِهِ ، فَهُوَ أَحَقُّ بِهِ مِنْ غَيْرِهِ " . قَالَ مَالِك فِي رَجُلٍ بَاعَ مِنْ رَجُلٍ مَتَاعًا ، فَأَفْلَسَ الْمُبْتَاعُ : فَإِنَّ الْبَائِعَ إِذَا وَجَدَ شَيْئًا مِنْ مَتَاعِهِ بِعَيْنِهِ أَخَذَهُ ، وَإِنْ كَانَ الْمُشْتَرِي قَدْ بَاعَ بَعْضَهُ وَفَرَّقَهُ فَصَاحِبُ الْمَتَاعِ أَحَقُّ بِهِ مِنَ الْغُرَمَاءِ ، لَا يَمْنَعُهُ مَا فَرَّقَ الْمُبْتَاعُ مِنْهُ ، أَنْ يَأْخُذَ مَا وَجَدَ بِعَيْنِهِ ، فَإِنِ اقْتَضَى مِنْ ثَمَنِ الْمُبْتَاعِ شَيْئًا فَأَحَبَّ أَنْ يَرُدَّهُ وَيَقْبِضَ مَا وَجَدَ مِنْ مَتَاعِهِ وَيَكُونَ فِيمَا لَمْ يَجِدْ أُسْوَةَ الْغُرَمَاءِ ، فَذَلِكَ لَهُ . قَالَ مَالِك : وَمَنِ اشْتَرَى سِلْعَةً مِنَ السِّلَعِ غَزْلًا أَوْ مَتَاعًا أَوْ بُقْعَةً مِنَ الْأَرْضِ ، ثُمَّ أَحْدَثَ فِي ذَلِكَ الْمُشْتَرَى عَمَلًا بَنَى الْبُقْعَةَ دَارًا أَوْ نَسَجَ الْغَزْلَ ثَوْبًا ، ثُمَّ أَفْلَسَ الَّذِي ابْتَاعَ ذَلِكَ ، فَقَالَ رَبُّ الْبُقْعَةِ : أَنَا آخُذُ الْبُقْعَةَ وَمَا فِيهَا مِنَ الْبُنْيَانِ ، إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَيْسَ لَهُ ، وَلَكِنْ تُقَوَّمُ الْبُقْعَةُ وَمَا فِيهَا مِمَّا أَصْلَحَ الْمُشْتَرِي ، ثُمَّ يُنْظَرُ كَمْ ثَمَنُ الْبُقْعَةِ وَكَمْ ثَمَنُ الْبُنْيَانِ مِنْ تِلْكَ الْقِيمَةِ ، ثُمَّ يَكُونَانِ شَرِيكَيْنِ فِي ذَلِكَ لِصَاحِبِ الْبُقْعَةِ بِقَدْرِ حِصَّتِهِ ، وَيَكُونُ لِلْغُرَمَاءِ بِقَدْرِ حِصَّةِ الْبُنْيَانِ . قَالَ مَالِك : وَتَفْسِيرُ ذَلِكَ : أَنْ تَكُونَ قِيمَةُ ذَلِكَ كُلِّهِ أَلْفَ دِرْهَمٍ وَخَمْسَ مِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ ، فَتَكُونُ قِيمَةُ الْبُقْعَةِ خَمْسَ مِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ وَقِيمَةُ الْبُنْيَانِ أَلْفَ دِرْهَمٍ ، فَيَكُونُ لِصَاحِبِ الْبُقْعَةِ الثُّلُثُ وَيَكُونُ لِلْغُرَمَاءِ الثُّلُثَانِ . قَالَ مَالِك : وَكَذَلِكَ الْغَزْلُ وَغَيْرُهُ مِمَّا أَشْبَهَهُ ، إِذَا دَخَلَهُ هَذَا وَلَحِقَ الْمُشْتَرِيَ دَيْنٌ لَا وَفَاءَ لَهُ عِنْدَهُ وَهَذَا الْعَمَلُ فِيهِ . قَالَ مَالِك : فَأَمَّا مَا بِيعَ مِنَ السِّلَعِ الَّتِي لَمْ يُحْدِثْ فِيهَا الْمُبْتَاعُ شَيْئًا إِلَّا أَنَّ تِلْكَ السِّلْعَةَ نَفَقَتْ وَارْتَفَعَ ثَمَنُهَا فَصَاحِبُهَا يَرْغَبُ فِيهَا وَالْغُرَمَاءُ يُرِيدُونَ إِمْسَاكَهَا ، فَإِنَّ الْغُرَمَاءَ يُخَيَّرُونَ بَيْنَ أَنْ يُعْطُوا رَبَّ السِّلْعَةِ الثَّمَنَ الَّذِي بَاعَهَا بِهِ وَلَا يُنَقِّصُوهُ شَيْئًا ، وَبَيْنَ أَنْ يُسَلِّمُوا إِلَيْهِ سِلْعَتَهُ ، وَإِنْ كَانَتِ السِّلْعَةُ قَدْ نَقَصَ ثَمَنُهَا ، فَالَّذِي بَاعَهَا بِالْخِيَارِ إِنْ شَاءَ أَنْ يَأْخُذَ سِلْعَتَهُ وَلَا تِبَاعَةَ لَهُ فِي شَيْءٍ مِنْ مَالِ غَرِيمِهِ فَذَلِكَ لَهُ ، وَإِنْ شَاءَ أَنْ يَكُونَ غَرِيمًا مِنَ الْغُرَمَاءِ يُحَاصُّ بِحَقِّهِ وَلَا يَأْخُذُ سِلْعَتَهُ فَذَلِكَ لَهُ . وَقَالَ مَالِك فِيمَنِ اشْتَرَى جَارِيَةً أَوْ دَابَّةً فَوَلَدَتْ عِنْدَهُ ، ثُمَّ أَفْلَسَ الْمُشْتَرِي : فَإِنَّ الْجَارِيَةَ أَوِ الدَّابَّةَ وَوَلَدَهَا لِلْبَائِعِ ، إِلَّا أَنْ يَرْغَبَ الْغُرَمَاءُ فِي ذَلِكَ فَيُعْطُونَهُ حَقَّهُ كَامِلًا وَيُمْسِكُونَ ذَلِكَ E353
hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Whichever man sells goods and the one who bought them becomes bankrupt, if the seller has not received anything from the price and he finds his goods in their exact state, then he has more right to them than anyone else. And if the buyer dies, then the seller is equal with the creditors.'

hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنِي يَحْيَى ، عَنْ مَالِك ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ ، عَنْ عَطَاءِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ ، عَنْ أَبِي رَافِعٍ مَوْلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ : اسْتَسْلَفَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بَكْرًا ، فَجَاءَتْهُ إِبِلٌ مِنَ الصَّدَقَةِ ، قَالَ أَبُو رَافِعٍ : فَأَمَرَنِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنْ أَقْضِيَ الرَّجُلَ بَكْرَهُ ، فَقُلْتُ : لَمْ أَجِدْ فِي الْإِبِلِ إِلَّا جَمَلًا خِيَارًا رَبَاعِيًا ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ : " أَعْطِهِ إِيَّاهُ فَإِنَّ خِيَارَ النَّاسِ أَحْسَنُهُمْ قَضَاءً " 1353
hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Abu Rafi', the freed slave of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ borrowed a young camel. Then camels from charity came to him. Abu Rafi' said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered me to repay the man his young camel. I said: I did not find among the camels except an excellent four-year-old camel. He said: 'Give it to him, for indeed the best of people are those who are best in repaying.'

hadiths.arabicText: وَحَدَّثَنِي مَالِك ، عَنْ حُمَيْدِ بْنِ قَيْسٍ الْمَكِّيِّ ، عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ : " اسْتَسْلَفَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عُمَرَ مِنْ رَجُلٍ دَرَاهِمَ ثُمَّ قَضَاهُ دَرَاهِمَ خَيْرًا مِنْهَا . فَقَالَ الرَّجُلُ : يَا أَبَا عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ ، هَذِهِ خَيْرٌ مِنْ دَرَاهِمِي الَّتِي أَسْلَفْتُكَ . فَقَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عُمَرَ : " قَدْ عَلِمْتُ وَلَكِنْ نَفْسِي بِذَلِكَ طَيِّبَةٌ " . قَالَ مَالِك : لَا بَأْسَ بِأَنْ يُقْبِضَ مَنْ أُسْلِفَ شَيْئًا مِنَ الذَّهَبِ أَوِ الْوَرِقِ أَوِ الطَّعَامِ أَوِ الْحَيَوَانِ مِمَّنْ أَسْلَفَهُ ذَلِكَ أَفْضَلَ مِمَّا أَسْلَفَهُ إِذَا لَمْ يَكُنْ ذَلِكَ عَلَى شَرْطٍ مِنْهُمَا أَوْ عَادَةٍ ، فَإِنْ كَانَ ذَلِكَ عَلَى شَرْطٍ أَوْ وَأْيٍ أَوْ عَادَةٍ ، فَذَلِكَ مَكْرُوهٌ وَلَا خَيْرَ فِيهِ . قَالَ : وَذَلِكَ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ " قَضَى جَمَلًا رَبَاعِيًا خِيَارًا مَكَانَ بَكْرٍ اسْتَسْلَفَهُ " . وَأَنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عُمَرَ اسْتَسْلَفَ دَرَاهِمَ فَقَضَى خَيْرًا مِنْهَا . فَإِنْ كَانَ ذَلِكَ عَلَى طِيبِ نَفْسٍ مِنَ الْمُسْتَسْلِفِ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ ذَلِكَ عَلَى شَرْطٍ وَلَا وَأْيٍ وَلَا عَادَةٍ ، كَانَ ذَلِكَ حَلَالًا لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ
hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Mujahid that he said: Abdullah ibn Umar borrowed some dirhams from a man, then repaid him with dirhams better than them. The man said: 'O Abu Abd al-Rahman, these are better than my dirhams that I lent you.' He said: 'I know, but I am pleased with myself about that.'

hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنِي يَحْيَى ، عَنْ مَالِك أَنَّهُ بَلَغَهُ ، أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ ، قَالَ فِي رَجُلٍ : " أَسْلَفَ رَجُلًا طَعَامًا عَلَى أَنْ يُعْطِيَهُ إِيَّاهُ فِي بَلَدٍ آخَرَ " ، فَكَرِهَ ذَلِكَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ . وَقَالَ : " فَأَيْنَ الْحَمْلُ ؟ " يَعْنِي حُمْلَانَهُ E354 1355
hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Malik: It reached him that Umar ibn al-Khattab said regarding a man who lent a man food on condition that he gives it to him in another city - Umar ibn al-Khattab disliked that and said: 'Where is the carrying?' meaning its transportation.
plainChains: Malik <- (unknown sources) <- report about Umar ibn al-Khattab (Balagh/Disconnected)

potential_issues.issue: CRITICAL: This is a BALAGH narration using 'balaghahu' (بَلَغَهُ) - 'it reached him' - without mentioning any chain or source
potential_issues.impact: Balagh narrations are considered very weak (munqati'/disconnected) because the entire chain is missing. We don't know who informed Malik, through how many intermediaries, or what the original source was. This is essentially hearsay, though it may represent general knowledge circulating in Madinah

potential_issues.issue: Even if the chain were known, this is a mawquf narration stopping at Umar ibn al-Khattab, not reaching the Prophet ﷺ
potential_issues.impact: This represents Umar's ijtihad on a commercial matter, not a prophetic ruling

Topics: Lending Food for Delivery in Another Location
Opinion of Umar ibn al-Khattab on Commercial Practices

hadiths.arabicText: وَحَدَّثَنِي مَالِك أَنَّهُ بَلَغَهُ ، أَنَّ رَجُلًا أَتَى عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عُمَرَ ، فَقَالَ : يَا أَبَا عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ ، إِنِّي أَسْلَفْتُ رَجُلًا سَلَفًا وَاشْتَرَطْتُ عَلَيْهِ أَفْضَلَ مِمَّا أَسْلَفْتُهُ . فَقَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عُمَرَ : " فَذَلِكَ الرِّبَا " . قَالَ : فَكَيْفَ تَأْمُرُنِي يَا أَبَا عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ ؟ فَقَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ : " السَّلَفُ عَلَى ثَلَاثَةِ وُجُوهٍ : سَلَفٌ تُسْلِفُهُ تُرِيدُ بِهِ وَجْهَ اللَّهِ فَلَكَ وَجْهُ اللَّهِ ، وَسَلَفٌ تُسْلِفُهُ تُرِيدُ بِهِ وَجْهَ صَاحِبِكَ فَلَكَ وَجْهُ صَاحِبِكَ ، وَسَلَفٌ تُسْلِفُهُ لِتَأْخُذَ خَبِيثًا بِطَيِّبٍ فَذَلِكَ الرِّبَا " . قَالَ : فَكَيْفَ تَأْمُرُنِي يَا أَبَا عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ ؟ قَالَ : " أَرَى أَنْ تَشُقَّ الصَّحِيفَةَ ، فَإِنْ أَعْطَاكَ مِثْلَ الَّذِي أَسْلَفْتَهُ قَبِلْتَهُ وَإِنْ أَعْطَاكَ دُونَ الَّذِي أَسْلَفْتَهُ فَأَخَذْتَهُ أُجِرْتَ ، وَإِنْ أَعْطَاكَ أَفْضَلَ مِمَّا أَسْلَفْتَهُ طَيِّبَةً بِهِ نَفْسُهُ ، فَذَلِكَ شُكْرٌ شَكَرَهُ لَكَ ، وَلَكَ أَجْرُ مَا أَنْظَرْتَهُ " 1356
hadiths.english_translation: Malik said: It reached me that when a man would sell a palm tree that had been pollinated, or a slave who had property, or a pregnant animal, and the buyer and seller would differ about the stipulation - the seller saying 'I stipulated it for myself,' and the buyer saying 'He sold it to me with it' - it is said to the seller: 'Bring proof of your stipulation,' or the buyer takes an oath and gets what he claims.

potential_issues.issue: CRITICAL: This is a BALAGH narration ('balaghahu' بَلَغَهُ) with completely missing chain
potential_issues.impact: Balagh narrations are very weak (munqati') as we don't know the source, number of intermediaries, or reliability of transmitters. This likely represents legal practice or custom in Madinah rather than established prophetic tradition

Topics: Burden of Proof in Commercial Disputes

hadiths.arabicText: وَحَدَّثَنِي مَالِك ، عَنْ نَافِعٍ ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عُمَرَ ، يَقُولُ : " مَنْ أَسْلَفَ سَلَفًا فَلَا يَشْتَرِطْ إِلَّا قَضَاءَهُ " 1357
hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Malik from Nafi' that he heard Abdullah ibn Umar saying: 'Whoever lends a loan, let him not stipulate anything except its repayment.'

hadiths.arabicText: وَحَدَّثَنِي مَالِك ، أَنَّهُ بَلَغَهُ ، أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ مَسْعُودٍ ، كَانَ يَقُولُ : " مَنْ أَسْلَفَ سَلَفًا ، فَلَا يَشْتَرِطْ أَفْضَلَ مِنْهُ ، وَإِنْ كَانَتْ قَبْضَةً مِنْ عَلَفٍ فَهُوَ رِبًا " . قَالَ مَالِك : الْأَمْرُ الْمُجْتَمَعُ عَلَيْهِ عِنْدَنَا : أَنَّ مَنِ اسْتَسْلَفَ شَيْئًا مِنَ الْحَيَوَانِ بِصِفَةٍ وَتَحْلِيَةٍ مَعْلُومَةٍ ، فَإِنَّهُ لَا بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ ، وَعَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَرُدَّ مِثْلَهُ إِلَّا مَا كَانَ مِنَ الْوَلَائِدِ ، فَإِنَّهُ يُخَافُ فِي ذَلِكَ الذَّرِيعَةُ إِلَى إِحْلَالِ مَا لَا يَحِلُّ ، فَلَا يَصْلُحُ ، وَتَفْسِيرُ مَا كُرِهَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ : أَنْ يَسْتَسْلِفَ الرَّجُلُ الْجَارِيَةَ فَيُصِيبُهَا مَا بَدَا لَهُ ، ثُمَّ يَرُدُّهَا إِلَى صَاحِبِهَا بِعَيْنِهَا ، فَذَلِكَ لَا يَصْلُحُ وَلَا يَحِلُّ ، وَلَمْ يَزَلْ أَهْلُ الْعِلْمِ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ وَلَا يُرَخِّصُونَ فِيهِ لِأَحَدٍ E355
hadiths.english_translation: Malik said: It reached me that Abdullah ibn Mas'ud used to say: 'Whoever lends a loan, let him not stipulate anything better than it, even if it is a handful of fodder, for that is riba.' Malik said: The agreed upon matter with us is that whoever borrows something of measurable or weighable items, it is not permissible for him to repay other than the same kind that he borrowed. He should not repay dates for wheat, nor wheat for dates, nor wheat of one type for wheat of another type. All of this is not permissible if there was a stipulation in the loan or a custom followed in it. If it was done as a favor from the borrower without any prior arrangement or custom, then there is no harm in it.
plainChains: Malik <- (unknown) <- Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (Balagh/Disconnected) + Malik's own statement

potential_issues.issue: CRITICAL: The report about Ibn Mas'ud is BALAGH ('balaghahu' بَلَغَهُ) with missing chain
potential_issues.impact: Very weak (munqati') - we don't know who transmitted this from Ibn Mas'ud to Malik or through how many intermediaries

potential_issues.issue: The second part is Malik's own juristic opinion about the consensus in Madinah
potential_issues.impact: This represents Madinan legal doctrine rather than direct prophetic transmission

hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنِي يَحْيَى ، عَنْ مَالِك ، عَنْ نَافِعٍ ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ ، أَنّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، قَالَ : " لَا يَبِعْ بَعْضُكُمْ عَلَى بَيْعِ بَعْضٍ " 1359
hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Abdullah ibn Umar that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'None of you should sell over the sale of another.'

hadiths.arabicText: وَحَدَّثَنِي مَالِك ، عَنْ أَبِي الزِّنَادِ ، عَنْ الْأَعْرَجِ ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ ، أَنّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، قَالَ : " لَا تَلَقَّوْا الرُّكْبَانَ لِلْبَيْعِ ، وَلَا يَبِعْ بَعْضُكُمْ عَلَى بَيْعِ بَعْضٍ ، وَلَا تَنَاجَشُوا ، وَلَا يَبِعْ حَاضِرٌ لِبَادٍ ، وَلَا تُصَرُّوا الْإِبِلَ وَالْغَنَمَ ، فَمَنِ ابْتَاعَهَا بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَهُوَ بِخَيْرِ النَّظَرَيْنِ بَعْدَ أَنْ يَحْلُبَهَا إِنْ رَضِيَهَا أَمْسَكَهَا وَإِنْ سَخِطَهَا رَدَّهَا وَصَاعًا مِنْ تَمْرٍ " . قَالَ مَالِك : وَتَفْسِيرُ قَوْلِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِيمَا نُرَى وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ : لَا يَبِعْ بَعْضُكُمْ عَلَى بَيْعِ بَعْضٍ : أَنَّهُ إِنَّمَا نَهَى أَنْ يَسُومَ الرَّجُلُ عَلَى سَوْمِ أَخِيهِ ، إِذَا رَكَنَ الْبَائِعُ إِلَى السَّائِمِ وَجَعَلَ يَشْتَرِطُ وَزْنَ الذَّهَبِ وَيَتَبَرَّأُ مِنَ الْعُيُوبِ وَمَا أَشْبَهَ ذَلِكَ مِمَّا يُعْرَفُ بِهِ أَنَّ الْبَائِعَ قَدْ أَرَادَ مُبَايَعَةَ السَّائِمِ ، فَهَذَا الَّذِي نَهَى عَنْهُ وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ . قَالَ مَالِك : وَلَا بَأْسَ بِالسَّوْمِ بِالسِّلْعَةِ تُوقَفُ لِلْبَيْعِ فَيَسُومُ بِهَا غَيْرُ وَاحِدٍ ، قَالَ : وَلَوْ تَرَكَ النَّاسُ السَّوْمَ عِنْدَ أَوَّلِ مَنْ يَسُومُ بِهَا ، أُخِذَتْ بِشِبْهِ الْبَاطِلِ مِنَ الثَّمَنِ ، وَدَخَلَ عَلَى الْبَاعَةِ فِي سِلَعِهِمُ الْمَكْرُوهُ ، وَلَمْ يَزَلِ الْأَمْرُ عِنْدَنَا عَلَى هَذَا 1360
hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Do not go out to meet the riders to buy from them, and none of you should sell over the sale of another, and do not artificially inflate prices, and a town-dweller should not sell for a desert-dweller, and do not tie up the udders of camels and sheep.'
